title.en: Invasions by Turkic powers and new powers

text.en:
Anu learned that rulers from beyond the north-west raided rich temples.
"Mahmud of Ghazni did," said her teacher.

In the early 11th century Mahmud of Ghazni raided northern India many times, attacking rich temples such as Somnath and carrying away wealth, but he did not set up lasting rule.
In 1192 Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan at the second Battle of Tarain and his general Qutb-ud-din Aibak later founded the Delhi Sultanate (1206).
Meanwhile new powers like the Chauhans, Paramaras, Chandelas and Cholas rose in different regions.

prompt.en: A friend says Mahmud of Ghazni founded the Delhi Sultanate. How will you reply?

points.en: Mahmud raided; Ghori won at Tarain.
